explain.say: Hold a fridge magnet near a spoon, a coin, a can and a pencil. Some jump to it, others ignore it completely. Is it because they are metal? Not quite! Let us sort them and find the real rule.

groups.ask: Why are some metals not magnetic?

faq.a: Iron, nickel and cobalt, and alloys that contain them, such as steel. These are attracted by magnets.

faq.q: Why are some metals not magnetic?
faq.a: In most metals the tiny magnetic effects of the atoms cancel out. Only iron, nickel and cobalt can line them up strongly.

faq.q: Why does a magnet stick to the fridge?
faq.a: The fridge door is made of steel, which contains iron, so the magnet attracts it.
No. Most metals, like aluminium, copper, gold and silver, are not attracted by a magnet.

faq.q: How do recycling centres separate cans?
faq.a: Big magnets lift out steel cans, which contain iron. Aluminium cans are not magnetic, so they are left behind.

facts: Iron, nickel and cobalt are the common magnetic elements; steel is magnetic because it is mostly iron.
Aluminium, copper and gold are not attracted by ordinary magnets.
